newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT shares rebound after poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT shares rebound after poll.

text.p: Shares in Czech telephone monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. jumped on Monday as bullish sentiment returned to the the Prague Stock Exchange after strong gains for the right in the first round of Senate elections.

SPT was up 124 crowns, 4.5 percent, to 2,879 at 1130 GMT (1230 local time) with dealers saying sharp declines in the company's share price last week made for a cheap buy into the most heavily capitalised share on the Prague bourse.
"SPT was oversold last week and it was very, very cheap," said Jan Sykora of Wood & Company.

At the weekend, the first round of voting for the Czech Senate gave Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) a commanding lead although turnout at just over one third of elegible voters was very low.

Despite the generally favourable reaction to the results on the market, Sykora cautioned that much remained to be fought for at the final round this coming weekend and said there had been little buying from foreign institutions.
"There is very little foreign institutional buying as a result of the elections. It's mainly domestic buying. This was just the first round and the (vote) isn't won yet," he said.
Most other shares on the PX50 index rose at Monday's price fixing with advancers beating decliners by 39 to eight.
